bug_semantics: Picklescan is a static pickle scanner whose threat model is denylist matching of GLOBAL/STACK_GLOBAL imports. numpy.testing._private.utils.runstring is an exec() synonym callable from pickle __reduce__; a payload returning (runstring, ("import os; os.system(...)", {})) executes arbitrary OS commands on pickle.load(). Until 0.0.25 that module was absent from the unsafe-globals denylist, so the scanner did not count it as an issue: originally scan_pickle_bytes only incremented issues_count on denylist hits, and by v0.0.24 _build_scan_result_from_raw_globals assigned unlisted names SafetyLevel.Suspicious without incrementing issues_count/infected_files. Callers that treat infected_files==0 as clean (as in the first-party PoC) then deserialize the undetected gadget.
flaw_origin: The incomplete denylist and default-allow matching were first written in c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e (Implement Pickle scanner). That commit added src/picklescan/scanner.py with _suspicious_globals (builtins/os aliases/webbrowser/HTTP clients only; no numpy.testing) and scan_pickle_bytes lines 83-90 that flag a global only if its module is in that map. Immediate parent 6a76b8c3ac67dc04181e600614ecf2a423cca326 is boilerplate with no scanner or pickletools denylist. Later rename to _unsafe_globals and the Suspicious/Dangerous split are refactors of the same gap, not a new first-write. The v0.0.25 fix adds the missing numpy.testing._private.utils entry.
